title: Good news
author: Mark Jurkowitz
thematic_categories: Press & Media Criticism, Journalism Theory & Practice
summary: Article discusses the concept of 'good news' or 'solutions journalism' and its challenges in gaining traction in mainstream media. Jay Rosen is identified as a leader of the civic journalism movement and is quoted on the prospects for solutions journalism.
excerpt: New York University journalism professor Jay Rosen is a leader of the civic journalism movement, an effort to foster dialogue between news outlets and their communities that is a kissing cousin of solutions journalism. Rosen says that as long as good news is viewed as a side-show by the mandarins of the mainstream media, it is doomed to failure. 'The elite of the profession has not been in the lead of this,' he says. 'Until you have the best minds and best institutions at work on this challenge, how do you know what the capacity of the press is?'
pull_quote: As long as good news is viewed as a side-show by the mandarins of the mainstream media, it is doomed to failure.
tags: newspaper clipping, public journalism, civic journalism, solutions journalism, 1990s

title: Brutal, reassuring and unvarnished
author: Margaret Sullivan
thematic_categories: Press & Media Criticism, Politics & Democracy, Technology & Digital Media
